newsitem.title: USA: Universal to lay off 500-600 -- report. [corrected 23:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Universal to lay off 500-600 -- report. [corrected 23:00 GMT]

text.p: Seagram Co Ltd's Universal Studio is planning to lay off 500 to 600 employees worldwide in the next several weeks, the New York Post reported Thursday.
The newspaper, citing a source close to the studio, said the layoffs could eventually total about 2,000 globally.
A Universal spokeswoman was not immediately available, and a Seagram spokeswoman had no immediate comment. Shares fell 9/16 to 38-3/16 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Seagram, which acquired 80 percent of Universal in April 1995 from Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd, has been streamlining the company and has changed upper management.
Universal recently laid off 115 in its production services group, or about 10 percent of the total. In May, it cut about 30 persons in its music unit.

In April 1996, Seagram Chief Executive Edgar Bronfman Jr. hired Frank Biondi, a former top executive at Viacom Inc, to run the unit. High-powered Hollywood agent Ron Meyer joined Universal as president and chief operating officer in August 1995. (corrects Bronfman's name and title; clarifies date of Meyer hiring.)
